Ligand-Enabled Chemo- and Regioselective Ir(I)-Catalyzed
Intermolecular Hydrocarbonation of Allenes: Access to Branched
Products with All-Carbon Quaternary Centers
Alejandro Rey, Andrés Arribas, José L. Mascareñas,* and Fernando López*
Abstract: An iridium complex featuring the perfluori-
nated bisphosphine ligand d<sup>F</sup>ppe can catalyze intermolec-
ular hydrocarbonation reactions of allenes with precise
control over the selectivity to yield highly valuable
branched products instead of the more common linear
derivatives. Using N-substituted 3-carboxamide pyrroles
as C─H donors, the reaction gives exclusively C-4
substituted products, while furan analogues yield C-2 sub-
stituted derivatives. β-Unsubstituted acrylamides can also
be used as C─H sources to give chiral skipped dienes. The
additions are equally efficient using monosubstituted and
1,1-disubstituted allenes, enabling the efficient formation
of products bearing tertiary and all-carbon quaternary
stereocenters. Moreover, a preliminary analysis with
chiral bisphosphinite ligands confirms the feasibility
of an enantioselective variant. Computational (DFT)
studies provide relevant insights into this remarkable
ligand-driven branched selectivity.
Introduction
The metal-catalyzed addition of C─H bonds across C─C
unsaturated systems is one of the most attractive bond-
forming strategies in organic synthesis, largely due to its
complete atom economy.<sup>[1–5]</sup> These reactions typically pro-
ceed via oxidative addition of the C─H bond to a low-valent
metal catalyst, followed by migratory insertion of the resulting
metal hydride intermediate into an unsaturated partner,
usually an alkyne or an alkene.<sup>[6–12]</sup> Surprisingly, despite their
widespread use in C─H functionalization processes, allenes
have been scarcely explored in this type of hydrocarbonation
reactions.<sup>[13–16]</sup> This deficit may stem from the perception
that their two cumulated C─C double bonds pose severe
chemoselectivity and regioselectivity challenges. However,
this unique structural feature should rather be viewed as
an opportunity to make products that are inaccessible using
alkene or alkyne partners.
In this context, in 2009, Krische reported a regios-
elective hydroarylation of benzamides with 1,1,-dimethyl
allene to yield achiral ortho-prenylated benzamides with
high selectivity (Scheme 1a).<sup>[17]</sup> More recently, Ackermann
demonstrated that both iron and nickel catalysts can also

respectively, using aryl ketones or benzimidazoles as C─H

exclusively produced the more sterically accessible, linear,
achiral product. Indeed, related hydroarylation methods that
yield synthetically more appealing branched, chiral products
have not been described.<sup>[21–26]</sup>
We recently found that an appropriate choice of the
ancillary bisphosphine ligand allows to control the selec-
tivity in Ir-catalyzed intramolecular cycloisomerizations of
heteroarene-tethered allenes, leading to different types of
heterocyclic structures.<sup>[27]</sup> Encouraged by these findings,
we wondered whether a suitable ligand tuning of the
catalyst could also allow us to overcome the intrinsic
steric bias of intermolecular hydroarylations to give linear
products and produce synthetically more relevant branched
isomers.

yield. Importantly, using allenes bearing two different alkyl
groups allows for building chiral products with all-carbon
quaternary stereocenters, such as 4ah–4aj. The reaction toler-
ates various functional groups at the allene chains, including
trialkylsilyl and benzyl ethers, as well as a tetrahydropyranyl

from 77% to 89%. Moreover, sterically more demanding
allenes, such as phenyl- and isopropyl-substituted allenes 2n
and 2o, reacted efficiently, delivering the expected products
4an and 4ao in good yields. Remarkably, the hydroarylation
of allenes bearing a pendant alkene unit (e.g., 2p and 2q) was
completely chemoselective toward the desired C─C double
bond of the allene, allowing the isolation of pyrroles 4ap and
4aq in very good yields. Likewise, the presence of a nitrile
or a challenging alkyne moiety on the allene side chain was
compatible with the process, and the desired products 4ar and
4as were obtained in good yields.<sup>[43]</sup>

99%). The same result was obtained with a pyrrole bearing
a bulky N-TBS group, which furnished 4eg in quantitative
yield.

Conclusion
In summary, we have discovered that switching from dppe to
d<sup>F</sup>ppe as an iridium ligand in allene hydroarylation reactions
not only triggers the reactivity but also allows an exquisite
chemo- and regiocontrol to give unusual, sterically congested
branched allylic products. The reaction is also effective with
furans, as well as with
\alpha { , } \beta { - }
unsaturated dialkylamides. Partic-
ularly interesting, using 1,1-disubstituted allenes, it is possible
to build challenging allylic all-carbon quaternary stereocen-
ters with good yields and excellent selectivities. Moreover,
a preliminary exploration of different chiral ligands allowed
us to identify perfluorinated bisphosphinite ligands, such
as Biphop-F, as suitable candidates for an enantioselective
variant. DFT computational analysis confirmed the critical
role of the perfluorinated ligand for the observed reactivity
and selectivity, which not only decreases the energy barriers
but also determines the regioselectivity of the process by
establishing subtle NCI’s between its fluorine atoms and the
pyrrole scaffold.
